summary.name: Futuristic UI (FUI) / HUD Design. Category: Digital and 3D Aesthetics. Supplemental, user-requested direction.
summary.visualIdentity: Dark backgrounds, fine wireframes, limited cyan or magenta accents, and readable monospaced data define the look. Panels, reticles, scales, maps, and progress rings each serve a defined function. Startup, scanning, acquisition, and feedback correspond to visible data changes.
summary.suitableUses: Explicitly suited to fictional interfaces and title sequences alone, and to hybrid HUDs showing meaningful data or signal readouts. Inferred from the listed combinations: operations dashboards, mission-control reports, and sensor or diagnostic sequences. Product demos and other subjects are unspecified.
summary.limitations: Avoid meaningless microtext, excessive spinning rings, and overexposed neon, and label all fictional data. Not every cyberpunk scene is a HUD. Palette contrast checks cover two-color pairs only, so composited frames need rechecking. Delaunator does not perform arbitrary 3D meshing, and Leaflet has no universal video export API.
summary.palette: Suggested palette, used only when no approved palette is supplied: background #0C1822, foreground #E7F4F3, and accent #55C7CF. Use one cyan accent or an approved magenta alternative, not both. Gradients are disabled. Foreground on background measures 15.933:1, and background-colored text on the accent measures 8.942:1. Supplied exact colors override these values.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Startup, scanning, acquisition, and locking should map to visible data events, with bloom applied only to selected luminous elements. Video derives all state from seekable composition time, while pointer and scroll input apply only to interactive delivery. Motion-017 is a good fit when components are separable. Motion-011, 012, and 015 are optional and need compatible content. Timing values are unspecified.
summary.audio: No fixed audio is specified. Music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence may each suit the topic, but none is mandatory. Honor explicit user choices first; otherwise propose a coherent direction and state assumptions without inventing assets. Waveforms should derive from supplied or precomputed audio.
summary.assetRequirements: Specific fonts, icons, reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are unspecified; the source treats them as optional examples. Monospaced fonts and other assets must load before rendering. All fictional data must be labeled. Map tiles and geographic data require authorization and attribution. Graph or triangulation inputs need finite, validated data with stable IDs.
summary.combinations: FUI works alone for fictional interfaces and title sequences. Add a hybrid when the HUD must show meaningful data. With style-097, D3 or Leaflet data panels use cyan strokes and bloom only on the active value. With style-063, cyan waveform traces stay inside bounded panels, not oscilloscope green. Both hybrids avoid added off-palette accents and decorative rings.
summary.productionApproach: HyperFrames is the primary pipeline for assembly, timing, audio sync, validation, and export. Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required output, and the reason must be recorded. Three.js with UnrealBloomPass, SVG, or D3 can render visuals, while Motion or GSAP can drive movement with one owner per property. Seed randomness, load fonts, and render from shared time. Verify key frames, decoded video, audio, and loop seams. Alternatives are Blender frame sequences with Remotion, or Remotion alone. Stack names are suggestions, not the source's actual toolchain.
